doc.title: Jimmy Lewis interviewed by Monk Rowe, New York City, New York, November 16, 1995

title: Growing up in Nashville and starting on ukulele
summary: Lewis, born in Nashville, describes the school and Fisk bands and learning ukulele from Professor Snead at about ten.

story.theme_name: Growing up and learning music: family, first instruments, teachers
story.community_name: Picking up a first guitar or banjo, self-taught

blocks.x: We are here today in New York filming for the Hamilton College Jazz Archive. My name is Monk Rowe and it’s a great pleasure to have bassist Jimmy Lewis with us. Welcome. You’re a Kansas City native?
Nashville. What was music like in Nashville when you grew up?

Well there was a lot of jazz around the schools you know, and they had some nice bands — Fisk University, a big band you know? And I started, I was around most of the good musicians that came, and so I met a guy that was going to Fisk. He was Professor Snead. And he played all the string instruments. He started me out on the ukulele. I started out on the ukulele. I was about ten years old. And I got to be pretty famous in and around town.
